output.headline: Applies for up to $11.3M in state ASSETS grant money for after-school programs at ten high schools
output.summary: Approves the district's application to the California Department of Education for $11,335,430 in 21st Century After School Safety and Education for Teens (ASSETS) funding for after-school programming at ten district high schools from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027. It also lets the Superintendent accept the money, in whole or in part, if it is awarded.

output.headline: Accepts $150,000 from the Eat.Learn.Play Foundation for Oakland Athletic League middle school sports
output.summary: Accepts a grant award of $150,000 in restricted funding from the Eat.Learn.Play Foundation for Oakland Athletic League middle school sports programming. The grant covers January 1, 2022 through December 31, 2022. The money must be used as described in the grant letter.

output.headline: Ratifies a five-year agreement with Alameda County districts on interdistrict attendance permits
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) sets the terms for issuing permits that let students living in Oakland attend school in other Alameda County districts, and the reverse. It is based on Education Code Section 46600 and covers the 2021-22 through 2025-26 school years. The text does not list any payment.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for a contractor's technical support on workflow software for newcomer social workers
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with a contractor to provide technical support for a smoother workflow in the software used by Newcomer Social Worker Teams. The district can pay up to $10,000 for January 24, 2022 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,593 for Axis Mundi to provide therapists at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Axis Mundi Center for Mental Health to provide therapists at Hoover Elementary School. They will work with students individually and in groups on social emotional learning skills, and will advise and train staff virtually. The district can pay up to $12,593 for January 10, 2022 through June 30, 2022.

vendor.name: Axis Mundi Center for Mental Health

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Reading Partners tutoring at Bridges Academy @ Melrose
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Reading Partners to provide a tutoring program at Bridges Academy @ Melrose. The district can pay up to $5,000 for September 1, 2021 through May 31, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $4,000 for a reading intervention provider at East Oakland Pride Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving, after the service period ended, an agreement with an individual contractor to provide reading intervention to 2nd through 5th graders who are two or more levels below grade level, using a literacy intervention program, at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The district can pay up to $4,000 for August 12, 2021 through January 12, 2022.

output.headline: Adds $21,000 and six months for Anthonio's inspections at Markham Elementary playmatting project
output.summary: This amendment adds $21,000 to the special inspection agreement with Anthonio, Inc., raising it from $36,100 to $57,100. It also extends the end date from December 31, 2021 to June 30, 2022 (181 more days), because some manufacturers could not deliver product on the original schedule. The project is the Markham Elementary School playmatting and accessibility project, paid from Measure J.

output.headline: Extends Ninyo & Moore's Fremont High construction consulting agreement to December 31, 2021
output.summary: This third amendment extends the Ninyo & Moore consulting agreement for the Fremont High School new construction project from August 17, 2021 to December 31, 2021. It adds no money. The new end date is before this vote, so the extension covers a period that had already passed.

output.headline: Awards G & G Builders $179,890 for playmatting and asphalt repair at Hintil Kuu Child Development Center
output.summary: G & G Builders will remove two play structures, repair asphalt with slurry seal, and install a new play structure and playmatting at the Hintil Kuu Child Development Center. The price includes a $15,000 general contingency allowance. Work is scheduled from March 10, 2022 to June 8, 2022 and is paid from Measure J.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for Lifelong Medical Care to connect Hoover Elementary families to health care
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Lifelong Medical Care to give Hoover Elementary School families information and connect them to medical and dental services, through a Navigator or the Community Schools Manager. The goal is to remove barriers that keep students from attending school. The district can pay up to $25,000 for January 3, 2022 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Pays Ninyo & Moore up to $175,645.80 for soil vapor and air testing at the Fremont High site through 2024
output.summary: Ninyo & Moore will keep sampling and reporting on soil vapor points, indoor air and outdoor air every quarter at the Fremont High School new construction site, at the request of the state's Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC). The limit includes up to $15,967.80 for any additional services. Work began January 3, 2022, before this vote, and runs through December 31, 2024.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for SPAAT to prepare to lead after-school programs at McClymonds High
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Student Program for Academic & Athletic Transitioning (SPAAT) to take part in the transition process for becoming the after-school lead agency at McClymonds High School for the 2022-2023 school year. The district can pay up to $5,000 for February 9, 2022 through June 30, 2022.

vendor.name: Student Program for Academic & Athletic Transitioning (SPAAT)

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost dance residency from Oakland Ballet for third graders at Oakland Academy of Knowledge
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, a no-cost agreement for Oakland Ballet to run its "You Can Dance" Residency Program for third grade students at Oakland Academy of Knowledge. The program uses dance to build creativity, problem solving and collaboration. It runs January 28, 2022 through March 4, 2022 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Reading Partners one-on-one reading help at Madison Park Academy Lower
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Reading Partners to give about 40 students, chosen by staff referral, a one-on-one reading intervention program at Madison Park Academy-Lower Elementary School. The district can pay up to $5,000 for August 9, 2021 through May 25, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Arts Connect program from the Museum of Children's Arts for teachers and school leaders
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, a no-cost agreement for the Museum of Children's Arts to provide its Arts Connect Program. The program supports teachers, school site leaders and teacher leadership teams in using art-centered learning, including arts and social emotional learning in the classroom and in staff training, and in sharing the results. It runs October 1, 2021 through September 30, 2022 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves a 2021-22 nonpublic school and agency services contract with Edgewood Center
output.summary: Approves a master contract with Edgewood Center for Children and Families, a nonpublic, nonsectarian school and agency, to provide services to special education students as set out in the contract. It covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and follows the terms of an earlier board resolution. The action text does not state a dollar amount, and the term began before the board vote.

vendor.name: Edgewood Center for Children and Families

output.headline: Approves up to $30,000 for Higher Ground to provide a school climate coach at East Oakland Pride
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Higher Ground Neighborhood Development Corp to provide a school climate coach at East Oakland Pride Elementary School, offering in-class support, gender-specific behavioral skill-building groups and general supervision. The district can pay up to $30,000 for August 12, 2021 through May 19, 2022. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost after-school drama class from Piedmont Performing Arts School at Thornhill Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, a no-cost agreement for Piedmont Performing Arts School to teach after-school classes two days a week at Thornhill Elementary School. The classes teach acting basics and drama games that build social skills, creativity and self-expression. It runs August 30, 2021 through May 25, 2022 at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Skill Struck computer science curriculum for an Allendale Elementary after-school class
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Skill Struck to provide curriculum and online professional learning support so an Allendale Elementary School instructor can teach an after-school computer science course to select 2nd and 3rd graders. The district can pay up to $5,000 for January 31, 2022 through May 20, 2022.

output.headline: Ends the district's after-school agreement with Health Initiatives for Youth at McClymonds High
output.summary: This resolution terminates the district's 2021-22 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Health Initiatives for Youth for after-school services at McClymonds High School. The text does not state a dollar amount or the reason.

output.headline: Accepts a $25,000 donor-advised fund grant from Fidelity Charitable for 2021-22
output.summary: The district receives $25,000 from Fidelity Charitable, a donor-advised fund, for the 2021-22 school year. The grant is to be used "where it's needed most," so the text names no specific program. The Chief of Staff's office brought the item.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $17,500 for Higher Gliffs to have an artist-in-residence paint a history mural at Fremont High
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Higher Gliffs for a community muralist and artist-in-residence to work with Fremont High School visual art students, the Performing Arts Department and the Media Academy. They will plan, prepare and paint a mural of the school's history in the Fremont Auditorium. The district can pay up to $17,500 for September 1, 2021 through June 3, 2022.

output.headline: Approves Personnel Report No. 2122-0007 from Talent/Human Resources
output.summary: Approves the Talent/Human Resources Department's Personnel Report No. 2122-0007, a routine report of staffing actions. The action text does not list the individual actions or any dollar amount.

output.headline: Pays Rigorous Love up to $9,303 for nine anti-racism staff workshops at LIFE Academy
output.summary: Rigorous Love will lead nine workshops or trainings for staff at LIFE Academy on what anti-racism looks like in a school. The agreement runs from November 1, 2021 through May 26, 2022 and is paid from donations. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

output.headline: Pays Oppenheimer Investigations Group up to $33,000 for Title IX legal services
output.summary: Oppenheimer Investigations Group will provide legal services to the district on Title IX matters, which cover sex-based discrimination and harassment. The agreement runs from January 15, 2022 through June 30, 2022. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Asian Youth Center up to $55,789 for mentoring and instruction support at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: East Bay Asian Youth Center will provide one-to-one mentoring, small group instruction and support for teachers and students at Urban Promise Academy during school hours. The goal is to improve teaching and learning and school culture. The agreement runs from October 1, 2021 through May 27, 2022 and is funded by Educate 78, Salesforce.org and Title 4 student support funds.

output.headline: Pays an activities coordinator up to $18,000 for break and lunch games at Elmhurst United Middle School
output.summary: An individual contractor will serve as Activities and Enrichment Coordinator at Elmhurst United Middle School. During morning break and lunch, the coordinator will run team-building games, playground games and sports skills activities. The agreement runs from November 1, 2021 through May 25, 2022, and the Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Cantare Con Vivo up to $4,998 for music instruction at La Escuelita Elementary
output.summary: Cantare Con Vivo will work with school staff to teach students music fundamentals in a step-by-step curriculum that supports language development and social studies. The agreement runs from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2022. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $54,682.50 for a job readiness class at Rudsdale High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will create a new elective class called Job Readiness at Rudsdale Continuation High School, meeting in person every Monday and Friday. It will also build partnerships, such as with Laney and Alameda community colleges, to give students more opportunities. The agreement runs from December 30, 2021 through June 30, 2022 and is paid from Measure N funds.

output.headline: Pays Candidly Speaking up to $1,000 for student discussion groups at Redwood Heights Elementary
output.summary: Candidly Speaking will meet with students in grades 3 to 5 at Redwood Heights Elementary to lead group discussions about current events and emotional well-being. The sessions also teach speaking and group skills. The agreement runs from January 18, 2022 through June 8, 2022, and the Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $16,000 for attendance outreach and counseling at Sojourner Truth Independent Study
output.summary: An individual contractor will provide attendance outreach, counseling, mentoring and referrals for students who need help with academics or attendance at Sojourner Truth Independent Study. The agreement runs from January 31, 2022 through June 30, 2022. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Cuts Cantare Con Vivo's Franklin Elementary music contract by $1,320 to $17,160
output.summary: This amendment reduces the Cantare Con Vivo agreement for music lessons at Franklin Elementary from $18,480 to $17,160 because fewer students will be served for the rest of the year. Lessons continue for TK through 2nd grade students in small groups and large assemblies. The end date also moves from May 25, 2022 to May 24, 2022.

output.headline: Adds $5,760 for a digital arts specialist at Community Day High through Oakland Public Education Fund
output.summary: This amendment adds six hours per week of a Youth Beat digital arts specialist to run the multimedia pathway program for Community Day High School students, starting January 2022. It raises the agreement from $20,000 to $25,760. The agreement runs from September 6, 2021 through May 27, 2022 and is paid from Measure N funds.

output.headline: Pays Museum of Children's Arts up to $16,870 for an artist residency at Laurel Elementary
output.summary: The Museum of Children's Arts will run an Artist Residency Program for grades 3, 4 and 5 at Laurel Elementary School. The program is aligned to California standards for visual and performing arts and is managed through the Academics and Instruction Department. The agreement runs from January 3, 2022 through June 30, 2022, and the Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Reading Partners up to $10,000 for reading tutoring at Fruitvale Elementary
output.summary: Reading Partners will run a reading tutoring program for selected students in grades 1 to 4 at Fruitvale Elementary School. The agreement runs from December 6, 2021 through May 25, 2022. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Destiny Arts Center up to $16,320 for weekly dance classes at Edna Brewer Middle School
output.summary: Destiny Arts Center will bring weekly dance and movement arts classes, including Creative Youth Development Framework classes, to all students at Edna Brewer Middle School. Each session is about an hour and is held over Zoom. The agreement runs from August 1, 2021 through May 31, 2022 and is paid from the Measure G1 parcel tax. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Pays Paul Dresher Ensemble up to $14,633 for music instruction at Elmhurst United Middle School
output.summary: Paul Dresher Ensemble will provide extra music instruction at Elmhurst United Middle School in strings, mariachi, percussion and jazz. The agreement runs from December 15, 2021 through May 31, 2022 and is paid from the Measure G1 parcel tax. The Board is approving it after the start date.

output.headline: Accepts up to 20 paid student internships from Nielsen at no cost to the district
output.summary: The Nielsen Company will launch a partnership offering up to 20 paid internships for students, run through the High School Linked Learning Office. The district pays nothing under this agreement. It runs from February 4, 2022 through February 4, 2023.

output.headline: Approves the 2022-23 funding application for the district's California State Preschool Program
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text calls the program CSSP while the title and the program's name use CSPP.
output.summary: This resolution certifies the Board's approval of the district's application to keep receiving state funding for the California State Preschool Program in 2022-23. The program is run by the Early Childhood Education Department and provides child care and development services. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Amends the 2022-23 classified staff layoff resolution for lack of funds or work
output.summary: Adopts an amendment to the resolution that lets the district reduce, reinstate, increase or create classified (non-teaching) positions for the 2022-23 fiscal year, based on lack of funds or lack of work shown in the budget process. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Approves 2022-23 school internet contracts with Sonic, AT&T and the county office, largest $354,500
output.summary: Approves three internet service contracts for the district: Sonic for internet and transport ($244,800, through June 2025), AT&T for transport to the Alameda County Office of Education ($103,615.20, through June 2025), and the county office for internet service ($354,500, through June 2027). The district's own projected share is only a small part of each contract ($12,240, $5,181 and $17,725, plus tax), and the contracts depend on E-Rate (a program that helps pay for school internet) and California Teleconnect funding.

vendor.name: Sonic; AT&T; Alameda County Office of Education

output.headline: Moves Kaboom!'s donated playspace from Horace Mann to Oakland Academy of Knowledge and adds Burckhalter
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title calls the school Oakland Academy of Knowledge, but the action text calls it Oakland School of Knowledge.
output.summary: Amends the district's agreement with Kaboom!, Inc., which donates and builds play spaces at schools. The play space planned for Horace Mann Elementary School will instead go to Oakland Academy of Knowledge, and Burckhalter Elementary School is added as another school that will receive one. No dollar amount is stated, and all other terms of the agreement stay the same.

output.headline: Approves up to $850,000 for Bay Area Transport Services to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Bay Area Transport Services for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $850,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $275,000 for Bay Area Wheelchair Transport to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Bay Area Wheelchair Transport LLC for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $275,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $150,000 for Bus Loop to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Bus Loop LLC for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $150,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $150,000 for Corinthian International Parking to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Corinthian International Parking Transportation Services for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $150,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $150,000 for Durham School Services to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Durham School Services for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $150,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $150,000 for Pronto Charters to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Pronto Charters for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $150,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $150,000 for Storer Transportation Service to run activity buses through 2026
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Storer Transportation Service for school activity bus service with seat belts, for Oakland Athletic League sports events and field trips. The district can spend up to $150,000 from August 9, 2021 through June 30, 2026. The service period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $105,000 for Isom Advisors' financial advice and bond disclosure work through 2025
output.summary: Approves an agreement with Isom Advisors, a division of Urban Futures, Inc., to provide financial advisory services and continuing disclosure services (the regular financial reports the district must provide to bond investors). The district can spend up to $105,000 from March 1, 2022 to March 1, 2025.

vendor.name: Isom Advisors, a Division of Urban Futures, Inc.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $80,000 for Moss Adams to audit Measure G and G1 parcel tax spending
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with Moss Adams to audit whether Measure G and G1 parcel tax money was spent only on the programs listed in the ballot language, and to audit those funds' financial statements for the year ending June 30, 2022. The district can pay up to $80,000 for the period July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,549 for an outside compliance audit of Measure N parcel tax spending
output.summary: The board is approving, after the term began, an agreement with an outside auditor to carry out a compliance audit of the revenues and expenditures of the Measure N parcel tax funds for the years ending June 30, 2020, 2021 and 2022. The district can pay up to $20,549 for the period January 11, 2022 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Adopts the Board's 2022-23 K-12 education budget letter and lets leaders sign and send it
output.summary: The Board adopts its annual letter on the K-12 education budget for 2022-23. It also authorizes the Board President and the Superintendent to sign the letter and send it on behalf of the district. No dollar amount is listed.

output.headline: Adopts the district's K-12 academic calendar for the 2022-23 school year
output.summary: The Board adopts the academic calendar for K-12 schools for the 2022-23 school year. The text does not list specific dates or any dollar amount.

output.headline: Adopts amendments to Board Policy 10000, the district's Conflict of Interest Code
output.summary: The Board adopts proposed changes to Board Policy 10000, the Conflict of Interest Code. The text refers to the specific changes as attached and does not describe them. No dollar amount is listed.
